cards.text: Solomon paints a picture: Wisdom is out in the street, lifting her voice in the square. She is not whispering, friend. She is NOT sending a polite little text.

cards.question: True or false: Wisdom saves her speech for a quiet room where only a few people can hear.

cards.text: Wisdom opens her speech with a question: "How long, O simple ones, will you love your simple ways?" That's the voice of somebody watching you hit snooze for the forty-seventh time.

cards.question: Wisdom calls out the simple ones. Who else does she call out in that same question?
Wisdom asks how long fools will ___ knowledge.

cards.text: Then Wisdom tells them what could have been. If they had repented at her rebuke, she says, "then surely I would have poured out my spirit on you"

cards.question: Wisdom says if they had repented at her rebuke, she would have poured out her spirit on them. What else would she have done?

answers.text: made her words known to them
made them rulers of the city

cards.text: But Wisdom called, and they refused. She held out her hand, and no one took it, which is like reaching down to help somebody up and they just STARE at your hand, except it's EVERYBODY.

cards.question: True or false: Wisdom says they took her counsel and only turned down her correction.

cards.text: Then the tone flips. Wisdom says, "in turn I will mock your calamity; I will sneer when terror strikes you"

Wisdom says their dread will come like a storm and their destruction like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish overwhelm them. That's not a drizzle, friend, that's the kind of weather that makes every phone in the room SCREAM.

cards.question: When distress and anguish overwhelm them, the people finally do something they refused to do before. What is it?
True or false: When the people earnestly seek Wisdom in their trouble, they find her.
Wisdom says the people hated knowledge and chose not to ___ the LORD.

cards.text: Wisdom says they accepted none of her counsel and despised all her reproof. So they will eat the fruit of their own way and be filled with their own devices.

cards.question: Wisdom says the people will eat the fruit of their own way. What does that mean?

answers.text: they get what their own choices bring
they finally have plenty to eat
someone else pays for their choices

cards.text: Wisdom says the waywardness of the simple will slay them, and the complacency of fools will destroy them. Complacency is ignoring the oven timer because you're SURE you've got time, and friend, I have eaten that burnt batch more times than I will ever admit.

cards.question: True or false: Wisdom ends her speech with a promise that whoever listens to her will dwell in safety, secure from the fear of evil.
